root_causes.description: The checkout container was killed and restarted ('Killing: Stopping container checkout' -> 'Started'), producing 3 container restarts in the 5m window. During the crash/restart the checkout server span error rate spiked to 0.92 while its served request rate collapsed to ~0.10 req/s, confirming the checkout pod is the failing service.

evidence.expected_baseline: checkout normally serves a substantially higher request rate; collapsed traffic indicates serving outage

evidence.observed_value: container checkout stopped/killed in namespace otel-demo
evidence.expected_baseline: no container kill events during steady state

root_causes.description: Checkout sits in the call path of multiple downstream dependencies (cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog); a crash-driven restart could manifest as downstream call failures. However, downstream services (payment) showed no error spike, so this is a weaker alternative explanation.

evidence.expected_baseline: 0.00 — downstream payment is healthy, arguing against a downstream-caused failure

root_causes.description: Alternative hypothesis that checkout latency rather than crashes drove the failure. No latency instrumentation evidence was collected in this window and CPU/memory stayed flat (cpu=0.05, memory=1e8 constant), making a resource-driven latency fault unlikely.

evidence.expected_baseline: stable ~0.05; no CPU saturation to explain latency
stable ~1e8 bytes; no memory growth to trigger OOM/latency

remediation_steps: Inspect the checkout Deployment/pod status and describe the checkout container to confirm the crash/restart cause (exit code, OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff).
Check container resource limits and recent spec changes to the checkout Deployment; roll back any recent change that triggered the kill/restart loop.
Review checkout container logs around 2024-01-15T13:59-14:06 for panic/fatal/startup errors and fix the failing start path.
Restore checkout replica availability and verify request rate recovers from ~0.10 req/s and error rate returns to ~0.00.
